headline: 7 contracts and roles catalogued across Ethereum and Arc; 28+ Bitcoin reserve addresses listed on transparency page; no dedicated cirBTC GitHub or audit PDF found.
short_headline: 7 EVM contracts across Ethereum and Arc

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search returned cirBTC token at 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E (ERC-20, FiatTokenProxy) with implementation at 0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd. Arc explorer not directly searchable; Arc contract address confirmed from Circle developer docs. DeFiLlama lists protocol.chains as 'Bitcoin' but the token is an EVM asset on Ethereum and Arc.

Canonical deployed-contracts doc found at https://developers.circle.com/assets/cirbtc-contract-addresses listing Ethereum mainnet 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E and Arc mainnet 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0, plus testnet addresses on Arc Testnet and Ethereum Sepolia. deployed_contracts_doc set to this URL.

No dedicated cirBTC audit PDF is linked on the protocol page or docs. The whitepaper states cirBTC uses 'the same FiatTokenV2_2 contract codebase that has been audited by third-party security firms' and 'No material contract code has been modified from the audited version used for USDC and EURC.' Specific audit reports for FiatTokenV2_2 (used by USDC/EURC) exist at circlefin/stablecoin-evm but were not directly linked for cirBTC. Recorded in unknowns.

No dedicated cirBTC GitHub repository recorded in protocol.github. Whitepaper references code as open-source and Etherscan source metadata references path '/Users/aloysius.chan/Repositories/circlefin/stablecoin-evm-private-eurc-mainnet-eth/' suggesting derivation from circlefin/stablecoin-evm. No broadcast/deployment artifacts fetchable without a pinned repo URL. Recorded in unknowns.

Two EVM chains confirmed: Ethereum (chainId 1) and Arc (Circle's own L1). Arc explorer at explorer.arc.io confirmed in Circle docs for 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0. Arc is not in the DeFiPunkd supported chainId list (supported: 1, 10, 56, 130, 137, 324, 8453, 42161, 43114, 59144, 81457, 534352, 11155111). DeFiLlama protocol.chains='Bitcoin' appears to refer to the underlying BTC collateral chain, not the EVM deployment chains. Bitcoin-layer addresses are reserve wallet addresses, not smart contracts.

No factory contract pattern applies. cirBTC uses a single FiatTokenProxy per chain (not a factory). MasterMinter contract is the only factory-like component; its address was not surfaced in this run — recorded in unknowns.

Administrative roles documented in whitepaper: Proxy Admin (upgrades implementation), Owner (assigns all non-proxy-admin roles), Blocklister, MasterMinter Owner, Minter, Pauser. Whitepaper states roles are protected by cold storage key management requiring cryptographic consensus of multiple individuals; no single individual has control. Actual addresses for Owner, Blocklister, Pauser, MasterMinter contract not surfaced from fetched on-chain data this run — recorded in unknowns.

All admin_addresses entries trace to fetched URLs: Circle developer docs (D2), Etherscan token page (D1), and cirBTC whitepaper (D3). Ethereum implementation address 0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd and constructor-arg initial implementation 0xe7b84D8846c96Bb83155Da5537625c75e42d6E42 both sourced from Etherscan page fetch. Bitcoin reserve addresses listed on circle.com/cirbtc are Bitcoin-native addresses (not EVM); they are noted in evidence but not placed in admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Discovery walk covered website, Circle developer docs, Etherscan token page, and cirBTC whitepaper PDF. 6 EVM contract addresses catalogued (Ethereum proxy, Ethereum implementation, Ethereum initial implementation, Arc token, Ethereum Sepolia testnet, Arc testnet) plus 28+ Bitcoin reserve wallet addresses published on the transparency page. Admin role structure (Proxy Admin, Owner, Blocklister, MasterMinter, Minter, Pauser) documented from whitepaper but specific addresses for those roles were not surfaced on-chain in this run.

evidence.shows: Official cirBTC product page; confirms token is live on Arc and Ethereum, backed 1:1 by BTC, issued by Circle International Bermuda Limited (CIBL); lists 28+ BTC reserve wallet addresses with balances as of 2026-09-28; total supply 5736.41530979 cirBTC; supply split: Arc 4952.39808229, Ethereum 784.0172275

Official Circle developer docs listing cirBTC contract addresses: Ethereum mainnet 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E, Arc mainnet 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0, Arc Testnet 0xf0C4a4CE82A5746AbAAd9425360Ab04fbBA432BF, Ethereum Sepolia 0x3a3fe695F684Bf9b9e43CF43C2b895Ea5e392bB3

Etherscan token page for cirBTC on Ethereum: contract 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E is a FiatTokenProxy (ZeppelinOS upgradeable proxy, Solidity 0.6.12), implementation 0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd; constructor arg initial implementation 0xe7b84D8846c96Bb83155Da5537625c75e42d6E42; max total supply 741.97128084 cirBTC; 110 holders; source code verified exact match; 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted' per Etherscan

cirBTC whitepaper: confirms Ethereum contract 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E and Arc contract 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0; architecture uses FiatTokenV2_2 + FiatTokenProxy + MasterMinter; admin roles: Proxy Admin (upgrades implementation), Owner (assigns roles), Blocklister, MasterMinter Owner, Minter, Pauser; roles protected by cold storage key management requiring multi-person cryptographic consensus; no single individual controls any admin role; Chainlink Proof of Reserve integration; issued by Circle International Bermuda Limited (CIBL)

unknowns: D3: No dedicated cirBTC audit PDF linked; whitepaper claims same FiatTokenV2_2 codebase as USDC/EURC was audited by third-party firms but specific audit report URLs for cirBTC are not published

D4: No dedicated cirBTC GitHub repository URL recorded; Etherscan source metadata references circlefin/stablecoin-evm-private-eurc-mainnet-eth path (private repo); public stablecoin-evm repo at github.com/circlefin/stablecoin-evm may contain same code but no pinned deployment artifacts for cirBTC found
D5: Arc (Circle's own L1) is not in DeFiPunkd's supported chainId list; Arc contract 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0 cannot be read via defipunkd.com/api/contract/read in this run
D6: MasterMinter contract address for Ethereum cirBTC not surfaced; needs on-chain read of masterMinter() on 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E

D7: On-chain addresses for Owner, Blocklister, Pauser, and Proxy Admin roles on Ethereum cirBTC not surfaced this run; needs defipunkd.com/api/contract/read calls for owner(), pauser(), blacklister(), and admin() on proxy address 0x72DFB2E44f59C5AD2bAFE84314E5b99a7cd5075E
D7: Corresponding admin role addresses for Arc cirBTC contract 0x171A4217b86A807A64eB94757Db6849fb4bDbAA0 not fetchable (Arc not in DeFiPunkd supported chains)

D8: Bitcoin-layer reserve wallet addresses (28+ addresses listed on circle.com/cirbtc transparency page) are UTXO addresses, not EVM contracts; excluded from admin_addresses but are material to reserve verification

protocol_metadata.about: Circle Wrapped Bitcoin (cirBTC) is an ERC-20 token issued by Circle International Bermuda Limited (CIBL) that allows institutional users to deposit native BTC via Circle Mint and receive an equivalent amount of cirBTC on Ethereum or Arc, with redemption reversing the process. Each cirBTC is backed 1:1 by BTC held in custody by Circle National Trust (a federally chartered OCC-supervised trust bank) and legally segregated from Circle's corporate assets. The smart contract architecture reuses Circle's audited FiatTokenV2_2 codebase (the same contracts powering USDC and EURC), with a FiatTokenProxy for upgradeability and a MasterMinter for minting controls; Chainlink Proof of Reserve provides on-chain attestation of BTC backing. Minting and redemption are permissioned to verified Circle Mint institutional customers, while secondary transfer of cirBTC is permissionless as a standard ERC-20.
